Project headers are labels, not controls. There is no open or close here, because the phone answers yes or no to what a machine proposed.

The cap keeps headers to 3 per machine, so B stays short, and a row's position answers where it runs without reading its meta line. A hides the other projects' running work behind a filter, and its chips get ambiguous once the same repo is active on two machines.

Its one session is in Needs you
Its sessions are in Needs you
Needs you comes first, across every project. Below it, one section per active project. A session shows once, and every row still names its machine.
A subagent hangs off its session on a tree line, so it sits in its parent's project and runs on its parent's machine. Finished ones fold into one line.
The project chip lists what is active on this machine. Picking one switches the view and stops nothing. Open and Close act on one project only.
The project menu lists only what is active on the machine chosen beside it. A session starts in exactly one project on exactly one machine.
Every session result names its machine and its project. Projects are results too, with their state, and a locked command says why.
The daemon refuses a fourth project. Open stays where it was, locked, with the daemon's reason and the way out.
The confirmation lists what stops, session by session, as the daemon reports it. The other projects are not touched.
The receipt says what stopped. A stop the daemon has not seen finish is unconfirmed, not failed.
The phone groups the same way as the drawer. Headers are labels: the phone answers gates and never opens or closes a project.
